original.title: Pozole Rojo
original.description: A festive red-chile pork and hominy stew from Jalisco and Guerrero, served with a spread of crunchy garnishes so everyone can top their own bowl.
ingredients: 3 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
1 tbsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 cans (25 oz each) white hominy, drained and rinsed
1 tsp ground chile piquín or red pepper flakes
steps: Place the pork, halved onion, 3 garlic cloves, bay leaves, salt, and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat to low, partially cover, and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the pork is nearly tender.
Meanwhile, toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 20 seconds per side, until fragrant but not burnt.
Soak the toasted chiles in 2 cups hot water for 20 minutes, until soft.
Blend the chiles and their soaking water with the remaining 3 garlic cloves, oregano, and cumin until completely smooth, then strain through a sieve.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the chile purée, and fry, stirring, for 5 minutes until it darkens slightly.
Remove the onion and bay leaves from the pot, then stir in the chile sauce and the hominy.
Simmer for 45 minutes more, until the pork is very tender and the hominy has bloomed; season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and serve with cabbage, radishes, onion, lime wedges, oregano, chile, and tostadas on the side.

original.title: Mole Poblano with Chicken
original.description: Puebla's celebrated dark mole: dried chiles, nuts, seeds, spices, and Mexican chocolate ground into a rich, complex sauce served over poached chicken.
ingredients: 4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup lard or vegetable oil, divided
3 tbsp sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
1 1/2 oz Mexican chocolate (such as Ibarra), chopped
steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion, garlic, salt, and water for 35 minutes until cooked through; remove the chicken and reserve the broth.
Toast the chiles in a dry skillet for 15–20 seconds per side, then soak in hot water for 30 minutes and drain.
Heat 2 tbsp lard in the skillet over medium heat and fry the almonds, peanuts, and sesame seeds until golden, about 3 minutes; remove to a bowl.
In the same fat, fry the raisins until puffed, then the tortilla and bread until crisp, and add them to the bowl.
Sauté the onion and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes, and add to the bowl along with the roasted tomatoes and spices.
Blend the soaked chiles with 2 cups of the reserved broth until very smooth, then strain.
Blend the nut, bread, and tomato mixture with 2 more cups of broth until smooth.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp lard in a large heavy pot over medium heat, add the chile purée, and fry, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes.
Add the nut purée, chocolate, sugar, and salt, then thin with 2 cups broth and simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Add the chicken to the sauce and simmer 10 minutes to heat through, thinning with broth if needed.
Serve sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds, with rice and warm tortillas.

original.title: Carnitas
original.description: Michoacán-style pork shoulder simmered in its own fat with orange and spices until meltingly tender, then crisped for tacos.
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
steps: Season the pork all over with the salt, cumin, and oregano.
Melt the lard in a large heavy Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the pork, onion, garlic, bay leaves, orange juice, orange peel, and water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the pork falls apart easily.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium, and cook for 15–20 minutes until the liquid evaporates and the pork begins to fry and brown in the fat.
Turn the pieces gently so they crisp on several sides, then lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Discard the onion, peel, and bay leaves and coarsely shred the pork.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, lime, and salsa verde.

original.title: Tacos al Pastor
original.description: Mexico City's favorite street taco: thin slices of pork marinated in guajillo chiles and achiote, seared hot and served with sweet pineapple.
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 1/2 lb boneless pork shoulder, sliced 1/4 inch thick
1/2 fresh pineapple, peeled, cored, and sliced into rings
steps: Toast the guajillo chiles in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes and drain.
Blend the chiles with the pineapple juice, vinegar, achiote, garlic, oregano, cumin, cloves, and salt until smooth.
Toss the pork slices with the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or griddle over high heat and grill the pineapple rings until charred on both sides, then chop them.
Add a little oil to the skillet and sear the pork in batches without crowding, 2–3 minutes per side, until caramelized and cooked through.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then chop it into small pieces.
Fill the warm tortillas with pork and top with pineapple, onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

original.title: Carne Asada
original.description: Northern Mexican grilled flank steak marinated in citrus, garlic, and chile, sliced thin for tacos or served with beans and grilled onions.
steps: Whisk together the orange juice, lime juice, olive oil, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Place the steak in a shallow dish or zip-top bag, pour the marinade over it, and refrigerate for 2 to 8 hours.
Preheat a grill to high heat and oil the grates.
Remove the steak from the marinade and pat off excess liquid.
Grill the steak for 4–6 minutes per side for medium-rare, until well charred.
Grill the green onions alongside for 2–3 minutes until softened and blistered.
Let the steak rest for 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Warm the tortillas on the grill and serve with the steak, green onions, and pico de gallo.

original.title: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
original.description: Grilled corn on the cob slathered with creamy mayo-crema, rolled in cotija cheese, and dusted with chile and lime, just like the street carts.
ingredients: 1/4 cup Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Preheat a grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the corn, turning every couple of minutes, for 10–12 minutes until tender and charred in spots.
Meanwhile, stir together the mayonnaise, crema, and garlic.
Spread the hot corn all over with the crema mixture.
Roll or sprinkle each ear with cotija cheese.
Dust with chili powder and sprinkle with cilantro.
Serve right away with lime wedges for squeezing.

original.title: Sopa de Fideo
original.description: A homey Mexican noodle soup of toasted thin pasta simmered in a tomato-chicken broth, a favorite comfort food in kitchens across the country.
ingredients: 7 oz fideo noodles or thin spaghetti broken into 1-inch pieces
steps: Blend the tomatoes, onion, and garlic with 1/2 cup of the broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the fideo and stir constantly for 3–4 minutes until the noodles are evenly golden brown.
Carefully pour in the tomato purée (it will splatter) and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining broth, cilantro sprig, and salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Remove the cilantro sprig, taste for salt, and serve topped with avocado, queso fresco, and lime.

original.title: Tinga de Pollo Tostadas
original.description: Shredded chicken stewed in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce from Puebla, piled onto crisp tostadas with beans, crema, and fresh toppings.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
2 to 3 chipotle chiles in adobo, plus 1 tbsp adobo sauce
steps: Simmer the chicken in the salted water for 20 minutes until cooked through, then cool and shred, reserving 1/2 cup of the broth.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, adobo sauce, and reserved broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the chipotle sauce and oregano and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer 5 minutes more until the sauce clings to the meat; season with salt.
Spread each tostada with refried beans and top with the tinga.
Finish with lettuce, crema, queso fresco, and avocado and serve immediately.

original.title: Agua de Jamaica
original.description: A ruby-red, tart-sweet hibiscus flower cooler that's one of Mexico's most beloved aguas frescas.
ingredients: 1 cup dried hibiscus flowers (flor de jamaica)
steps: Rinse the hibiscus flowers briefly in a strainer to remove any dust.
Bring 4 cups of the water to a boil in a saucepan, add the flowers, and boil for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the sugar until dissolved, and steep for 15 minutes.
Strain into a large pitcher, pressing on the flowers, and discard them.
Add the remaining 4 cups cold water and the lime juice, then taste and adjust sweetness.
Chill thoroughly and serve over ice.

original.title: Champurrado
original.description: A thick, warming chocolate atole thickened with masa and sweetened with piloncillo, traditionally sipped alongside tamales in the cold months.
ingredients: 4 oz piloncillo, chopped, or 1/2 cup packed dark brown sugar
steps: Whisk the masa harina into the water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Heat the milk with the cinnamon stick and piloncillo in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming and the sugar dissolves.
Add the chocolate and whisk until melted.
Slowly pour in the masa mixture, whisking constantly.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, whisking often, for 8–10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Remove the cinnamon stick, add the salt, and serve hot.

original.title: Conchas
original.description: Soft, slightly sweet Mexican breakfast buns crowned with a crackly sugar topping scored to look like a seashell.
ingredients: 1/3 cup cold butter or vegetable shortening
1 tbsp cocoa powder (optional, for half the topping)
steps: Stir the yeast and 1 tbsp of the sugar into the warm milk and let stand 10 minutes until foamy.
In a stand mixer, combine the yeast mixture with the remaining sugar, eggs, butter, vanilla, and salt.
Gradually add the flour and knead with the dough hook for 8–10 minutes until the dough is smooth and slightly tacky.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll into balls, and space them on two parchment-lined baking sheets.
For the topping, mix the flour, powdered sugar, butter, and vanilla into a smooth paste; knead cocoa into half if you like.
Divide the topping into 12 portions, flatten each into a thin disc, and press one onto each bun.
Score the topping with a knife in a curved shell pattern.
Cover loosely and let rise for 45 minutes until puffy.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 18–20 minutes until the bottoms are golden, then cool on a rack.

original.title: Arroz con Leche
original.description: Creamy Mexican rice pudding perfumed with cinnamon and lime peel, enjoyed warm or chilled.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Combine the rice, water, cinnamon stick, and lime peel in a heavy saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, uncovered, for about 10 minutes until most of the water is absorbed.
Stir in the milk, evaporated milk, sugar, and salt.
Simmer over low heat, stirring frequently, for 25–30 minutes until the rice is very tender and the pudding is creamy.
Remove the cinnamon stick and lime peel and stir in the vanilla and raisins.
Serve warm or chilled, dusted with ground cinnamon.

original.title: Flan Napolitano
original.description: Mexico's silky, dense caramel custard made with condensed and evaporated milk and a touch of cream cheese.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and set a kettle of water to boil.
Cook the sugar and water in a small saucepan over medium heat, swirling but not stirring, until it turns a deep amber, about 8–10 minutes.
Immediately pour the caramel into a 9-inch round cake pan or flan mold and tilt to coat the bottom.
Blend the condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream cheese, eggs, vanilla, and salt until completely smooth.
Pour the custard through a strainer onto the set caramel.
Cover the pan with foil and set it in a larger roasting pan, then add hot water to come halfway up the sides.
Bake for 55–65 minutes, until the edges are set and the center jiggles slightly.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Run a thin knife around the edge, invert onto a rimmed platter, and let the caramel pour over the top.

original.title: Birria de Res
original.description: Jalisco-style beef slow-braised in an adobo of dried chiles and warm spices, served as a rich stew or with its consommé for dipping tacos.
ingredients: 4 lb beef chuck roast and bone-in short ribs, cut into large chunks
6 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Season the beef all over with the salt.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes per side; set aside.
Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side and simmer them with the tomatoes, onion, and garlic in water for 10 minutes until soft.
Drain and blend the chiles and vegetables with the vinegar, oregano, cumin, cinnamon, cloves, pepper, and 1 cup broth until smooth, then strain.
Return the beef to the pot, pour the adobo over it, and add the bay leaves and remaining broth.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat (or in a 325°F / 165°C oven) for 3 to 3 1/2 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Remove the beef, shred it, and discard the bones; skim the fat from the broth and season the consommé with salt.
Serve the beef in bowls with consommé, or dip tortillas in the fat, fill with beef, and griddle until crisp for quesatacos-style tacos.
Garnish with onion, cilantro, and lime, with a cup of hot consommé on the side.

original.title: Salsa Verde (Roasted Tomatillo Salsa)
original.description: A bright, tangy green salsa of charred tomatillos, serrano chiles, garlic, and cilantro for tacos, chips, and enchiladas.
ingredients: 1/2 cup cilantro leaves and tender stems
steps: Heat the broiler with a rack 4 inches from the element.
Spread the tomatillos, chiles, onion, and garlic on a foil-lined baking sheet.
Broil for 5–7 minutes, turn everything over, and broil 4–5 minutes more until charred and soft.
Peel the garlic and stem the chiles once cool enough to handle.
Blend everything, including the tomatillo juices, with the cilantro and salt to a slightly chunky purée.
Stir in the lime juice, taste for salt, and let cool before serving.

original.title: Chiles Rellenos
original.description: Roasted poblano peppers stuffed with melting cheese, dipped in a fluffy egg batter, fried golden, and served in a light tomato caldillo.
ingredients: 12 oz Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese, cut into thick sticks
steps: Roast the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under the broiler, turning, until blackened all over, about 8–10 minutes.
Place them in a covered bowl for 10 minutes to steam, then rub off the skins.
Cut a slit down one side of each pepper, carefully remove the seeds, and stuff with cheese; close with a toothpick if needed.
For the sauce, blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and broth until smooth, then simmer in 1 tbsp oil with the salt for 10 minutes.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold in the yolks one at a time and the salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Dredge each stuffed pepper in flour, shake off the excess, and dip it in the egg batter to coat.
Fry the peppers 2 at a time, spooning oil over the tops, for 2–3 minutes per side until golden; drain on paper towels.
Spoon the tomato sauce onto plates and set the chiles rellenos on top to serve.

original.title: Pescado a la Veracruzana
original.description: Veracruz's signature fish dish of white fillets baked in a tomato sauce with olives, capers, and pickled jalapeños.
ingredients: 4 white fish fillets (6 oz each), such as red snapper or cod
1 1/2 lb ripe tomatoes, chopped (or 1 can, 28 oz, diced tomatoes)
3 pickled jalapeños, sliced, plus 1 tbsp brine
steps: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice and set aside while you make the sauce.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaves, and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the olives, capers, jalapeños, and brine and season the sauce with salt.
Nestle the fish fillets into the sauce and spoon some sauce over the top.
Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with white rice.
